name: Borrowed notes
opensWhen: The player takes a classmate's compressed notes to prepare for the first unit test and does not give them back that week.
note: SCHOOL_AND_PROGRESSION.md, 'Notes need translation' (innovation 6) and the same-evening-unequal-time idea (innovation 3). A debt of attention, not of money. Authored draft: the owner edits every line (ROADMAP M3-12).

roles.name: The classmate who lent the notes

expression.observe: Their notes sit in your bag, written in a shorthand you only half follow. They have not asked for them back.
They mention, lightly, that they need the notes for their own revision before the next test.
They stop saving you the seat at the back. A short message asks whether you still have the notes.
In front of two others they say the notes were a favour, and that the favour has become a problem.
The notes go back with a proper thank-you. The favour closes cleanly and neither of you mentions it again.
You sit down together and turn their shorthand into something both of you can use. They find a gap in their own method while explaining it.
The notes stay in your bag until neither of you mentions them. The seat beside you is only a seat now.
'No hurry,' they say, in the tone people use when there is a hurry.
